title: Define and render a named customer artifact with a selected release owner

setupFiles.monochange.toml:
[defaults]
parent_bump = "patch"
[package."@acme/api"]
path = "packages/api"
type = "npm"
[package."@acme/ui"]
path = "packages/ui"
type = "npm"
[package."@acme/tokens"]
path = "packages/tokens"
type = "npm"
[group.main]
packages = ["@acme/api", "@acme/ui", "@acme/tokens"]
version_format = "primary"
[ecosystems.npm]
enabled = true
[lints.rules]
"npm/workspace-protocol" = "off"

[changelog.types]
feature = { bump = "minor", section = "feat", description = "Customer-visible features", stream = "user" }
fix = { bump = "patch", section = "fix", description = "Developer fixes" }
[changelog.streams.user]
description = "Customer updates"
setupFiles..changeset/customer.md:
---
"@acme/ui": feature
---

Save profile links for later.

prompt: Add a changelog output named launch_card for the user stream and main group, in monochange format with release mode and path product-notes/{{ version }}.md. Render that named output into review/launch-card.md using the CLI. Include the customer feature and exclude developer internals. Leave all changesets and manifest versions intact; we are drafting the customer announcement only.
expectation: The persisted named output selects user/main with the requested path/format/mode. CLI rendering writes customer feature notes only, without preparing or consuming changesets.

checks.why: The recurring output must persist its requested target, stream, path, format, and mode.
The final configuration and pending changesets must resolve.

checks.command: monochange notes --output launch_card --target main | node -e 'const fs=require("node:fs"),a=require("node:assert/strict"),s=fs.readFileSync(0,"utf8");a.ok(s.includes("Save profile links"));a.ok(!s.includes("RequestOptions"));'
checks.why: Named output selection must obey its audience stream.
The requested local artifact must exist.
The saved artifact must retain the selected audience.
Drafting announcements must not consume pending changesets.
Evaluation is limited to local planning and preparation; registry, tag, release, and push operations are outside the task.
